searchText: I feel like there are simplifications that can come, like not needing to do stack checks at runtime Though that only _really_ happens if EOF becomes mandatory i relistened to yesterday's discussion about that in EOF implementers call i think the point that was explained is that by keeping strict separation between code and data it's possible to compile an EOF contract directly to a circuit so my question was slightly off. it's not a point about zkEVMs, it's more about snarkifying EOF code i've created an issue to discuss enabling EXTCODE* opcodes in EOF, since we've been struggling to come to a consensus during calls i've tried to address all the concerns i've heard. please let me know if there are any that i missed https://github.com/ipsilon/eof/issues/169 > It's possible developers may use Legacy contracts as data storage via EXTCODECOPY. If this is a problem to the network I believe it should be addressed by more accurately pricing the opcode. sounds like EOF encourages developers to write data contracts in legacy code? how about EOFDATACOPY? [i agree](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1167#issuecomment-2395254594) but i don't wanna drop so many bombs at once 😬
